questions.question: Describe Weber's three types of authority and evaluate their usefulness.

points.text: Traditional: custom (monarchy). Charismatic: personality (MLK). Rational-legal: rules (elected officials). Evaluation: useful but some leaders combine types. Charismatic brings change but is unstable; rational-legal is stable but may resist change.

questions.question: Compare Marxist and Functionalist views of the state.

points.text: Marxist: state serves ruling class (protects property, maintains capitalist order). Functionalist: state serves everyone (maintains order, provides services). Evidence supports Marxist view but the state also provides welfare that benefits the working class.

questions.question: Evaluate whether democracy ensures that power is equally distributed.

points.text: Democracy gives formal equality (one vote) but real power is unequal: wealth funds parties, media shapes opinion, lobbyists influence policy. Marxists: democracy is a sham. Pluralists: democracy works through competing groups. Conclusion: some distribution but significant inequalities remain.
